business_problem: LexisNexis needed an AI retrieval architecture that could preserve relationships and time context across fast-changing financial and commodities data, because standard RAG could not produce reliable answers for high-stakes decisions.
solution_summary: LexisNexis Risk Solutions used MongoDB Atlas as the single store of truth for a time-aware reasoning platform built by its Maverick team. Instead of relying on standard RAG pipelines that treat facts as isolated text chunks, the team modeled nodes, relationships, vectors, and ontology as native MongoDB collections so the system could scale beyond the limits of out-of-the-box graph tooling. Every fact carries explicit start and end dates, allowing the database to pre-filter results into chronologically correct timelines before anything reaches the model. That architecture preserves ownership changes, temporal relationships, and other structural context that ordinary semantic search misses. Atlas therefore serves not only as persistent storage for the graph-shaped knowledge base, but also as the mechanism that grounds answers in history-aware evidence. By eliminating synchronization between separate graph, vector, and application layers, LexisNexis created a more accurate AI system for financial and commodities intelligence.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores nodes, relationships, vectors, and ontology collections as the single store of truth for time-aware reasoning.

data_flow: Articles, commodities facts, nodes, relationships, vectors, and ontology data are stored as MongoDB collections with time bounds; queries filter those collections into chronologically valid timelines before grounded results are handed to downstream reasoning and answer-generation steps.
business_outcome: LexisNexis eliminated synchronization tax between disconnected AI stores, improved answer accuracy for time-sensitive market intelligence, and created a scalable platform that can reason over large, changing financial datasets.
